title: Guide: MUSes by shrinking
description: An unsatisfiable seed is shrunk to a MUS by dropping clauses while the check still fails; the MUS and every superset leave the map. Satisfiable seeds are still blocked one at a time. See the guide page "MARCO: two kinds of answer".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Random CNF: 4 variables, 10 clauses. 7 MUSes, 12 MSSes (brute force).
neg(1,c).
neg(2,b).
pos(3,b).
pos(4,b). pos(4,d). pos(4,a).
pos(5,d).
neg(6,a).
neg(7,d). neg(7,b). pos(7,c).
neg(8,d).
pos(9,a). pos(9,c).
neg(10,d).
% The instance (Instances tab): pos(C,V) and neg(C,V) are the literals of clause C.
cl(C) :- pos(C,_).
cl(C) :- neg(C,_).
var(V) :- pos(_,V).
var(V) :- neg(_,V).
fragments.description: Part of the library example marco.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The map: a seed is any set of clauses (pick/1) not yet explored. Grown seeds (MSSes) block
% their subsets, shrunk seeds (MUSes) block their supersets; the map learns only these clauses.
{ pick(C) : cl(C) }.
% Maximal seeds first (Liffiton and Malik's getUnexploredMax): with --heuristic=Domain the
% solver decides every pick to true first.
#heuristic pick(C) : cl(C). [1,true]
#show pick/1.
fragments.description: Part of the library example marco.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: Part of the library example marco.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% Is the seed satisfiable? An assignment that satisfies every picked clause.
{ t(V) } :- var(V).
sat(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
sat(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
:- pick(C), not sat(C).
#show t/1.
fragments.description: Part of the library example marco.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction    options "--heuristic=Domain"
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Unsatisfiable: shrink to a MUS, report it, and remove it and its supersets from the map.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    E = G(M)
    if C.solve(assume E):
        A.add(G.block(M))
    else:
        for a in E:
            if a.true and not C.solve(assume E.flip(a)): E = E.flip(a)
        accept A.solve(assume E)
        A.add(G.above(E))
